subject: Maths
title: Inequalities in two variables
subtitle: Linear Inequalities · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can represent and identify regions defined by linear inequalities in two variables.

key_vocab.definition: An inequality in two variables such as y region on a coordinate grid, not just a line.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can represent and identify regions defined by linear inequalities in two variables.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: inequality in two variables -- An inequality in two variables such as y region on a coordinate grid, not just a line.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Draw the boundary line, choose dashed or solid, then test a point to determine which side to shade.
y ≤ mx + c ⇒ solid line, shade below
Solid line includes the boundary; shade the correct side

Key examples:
  ✓ y < x + 3: region below the line y = x + 3  (dashed line)
  ✓ y ≥ 2x − 1: region above and including the line  (solid line)
  ✓ x + y ≤ 5: test (0,0) gives 0 ≤ 5, true, so shade that side  (test point method)
  ✗ y < x + 3 uses a solid boundary line  (strict inequality = dashed)
  ✗ The line y = x is always the boundary for y > x  (y = x is correct boundary, but y > x is above)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – identifying the region
  Describe the region y < x + 2
  Boundary line: y = x + 2 (dashed, as strict <)
  Test (0, 0): 0 < 0 + 2 = 2, true
  Region: below the dashed line y = x + 2
  Below dashed line y = x + 2
  (Use a test point to verify which side satisfies the inequality.)

Example 2 – solid boundary
  Describe the region y ≥ 3x − 1
  Boundary: y = 3x − 1 (solid, as ≥)
  Test (0, 0): 0 ≥ −1, true
  Region: above and on the solid line
  Above/on solid line y = 3x − 1
  (Solid line means points ON the line are included.)

sections.title: Identifying boundary lines
sections.content:
State the boundary line and whether it is dashed or solid.

(a) y < 3x + 1
(b) y ≥ x − 4
(c) x + y ≤ 10
(d) 2x + y > 6

sections.title: Test point method
sections.content:
Test (0, 0). Is it in the region?

(a) y < x + 5
(b) y > 2x + 3
(c) x + y ≤ 4
(d) 3x − y ≥ 1

sections.title: Describing regions
sections.content:
Describe the region (above/below, left/right of boundary).

(a) y > 2
(b) x ≤ 5
(c) y < −x + 3
(d) y ≥ &frac{1}{2}x

sections.title: Checking points
sections.content:
Determine if the given point satisfies the inequality.

(a) (1, 4) in y ≤ 3x + 2?
(b) (3, 1) in y > x − 1?
(c) (2, 3) in x + y < 6?
(d) (−1, 2) in y ≥ 2x + 5?

sections.title: Combined regions
sections.content:
Describe the region satisfying all given inequalities.

(a) y ≥ 0, x ≥ 0, x + y ≤ 4
(b) x > 1, y  x
(c) y ≤ x + 2, y ≥ 0, x ≤ 3
(d) x + y ≤ 8, x ≥ 2, y ≥ 1
(e) y  −1, x < 3

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ A strict inequality () uses a dashed boundary line
✗ y < x + 3 means the region above the line y = x + 3
✓ Testing (0, 0) tells you which side of the line to shade
✓ ≤ and ≥ both use solid lines because the boundary is included
✗ y ≥ 2x means the region below the line y = 2x

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Identifying boundary lines:
  (a) y = 3x + 1, dashed
  (b) y = x − 4, solid
  (c) x + y = 10, solid
  (d) 2x + y = 6, dashed

Test point method:
  (a) 0 < 5, yes
  (b) 0 > 3, no
  (c) 0 ≤ 4, yes
  (d) 0 ≥ 1, no

Describing regions:
  (a) Above the line y = 2
  (b) Left of and on the line x = 5
  (c) Below the line y = −x + 3
  (d) Above and on the line y = &frac{1}{2}x

Checking points:
  (a) 4 ≤ 5, yes
  (b) 1 > 2, no
  (c) 5 < 6, yes
  (d) 2 ≥ 3, no

Combined regions:
  (a) Triangle with vertices (0,0), (4,0), (0,4)
  (b) Region above y = x, below y = 5, right of x = 1
  (c) Triangle-like region
  (d) Enclosed region
  (e) Region between y = −1 and y = 2x, left of x = 3
